## Punishments for making defamatory speeches \[Chapter 258\]

\[Full title: Punishments for making defamatory speeches and committing other offences (*vākpāruṣya*)\]

***Fire-god said*****:**

1\. If a person abuses the sick and men having defective organs, by means of lampoons, whether true or untrue or otherwise, he should be fined thirteen and a half *paṇas*.

2\. The king should levy a fine of twenty-five (*paṇas*) on one that abuses another (with the words) “I copulate with your sister or (I copulate with your) mother”.

3\. A punishment should be awarded after due consideration of the higher or lower caste. (A man of the higher caste committing adultery (on women) of the lower caste (should be levied) half (the fine) and (a man of the lower caste committing adultery) on (women) of the higher caste (should be levied) double (the fine).

4\. The men of lower orders of castes censuring the men of the next higher order should be levied double or three times the fine. But in the case of censures made by men of the higher orders on those of lower orders, half the fine should be levied.

5\. The fine (that should be levied) on a capable person uttering words threatening the injury of the hands, neck, eyes and thighs (of another) should be levied (the *sāhasa*) fine. It is half the fine, if it relates to the foot, nose, ear and arms.

6\. An incapable person who says as above should be levied a fine of ten *paṇas*. So also a capable person should give surety for the safety of that person.

7\. The middle *sāhasa* fine should be levied on that person who abuses one ascribing degrading sin (to him). The first kind of *sāhasa* should be levied on one who ascribes (another) with minor sin of second degree.

8\. The highest *sāhasa* (should be levied) for offences villifying the brahmins, kings and gods. Middle (*sāhasa*) (should be levided for offences villifying) one’s own relatives and the members of the village assembly and the first (*sāhasa*) (for speaking ill of one’s own) village or country.

9\. In the case of charge of murder without witness, (the judge) should pronounce (the judgement) after considering the marks, reasoning and written testimony, in order to safeguard (himself) from being misled by false marks.

10\. The fine for touching (another) with ashes, mud or dust is said to be ten *paṇas* and for touching with filth or the heels or spitting, double (that).

11\. (For offences against women) of one’s own (caste) single (fine should be levied) and twice that in the case of other women as well as of higher castes. The fine is half in the case of (offences against those) belonging to lower castes. (For offences done) under delusion or the influence of liquor, (there is) no punishment.

12\. The organ of a non-brahmin that inflicts pain on a brahmin should be cut off. First (*sāhasa*) punishment (should be preseribed) for one who raises (one’s arms and strikes a brahmin) and half that (fine) if one touches.

13\. If the hand and the leg are held and pulled, the fine is ten and twenty (*paṇas*) respectively. If (several men) one by one (hold and pull), the scriptures (prescribe) the middle *sāhasa* for all of them.

14\. The fine for pulling the feet or hair or the garment or hand is ten *paṇas*. The fine for causing affliction or pulling or dragging after putting cloth around or placing foot (on a person) is one hundered (*paṇas*).

15\. One who causes misery by means of a log of wood etc. and (if there be) no blood (injury), should be fined thirtytwo *paṇas*. Double that (is the fine), if blood is seen.

16-17. The middle (*sāhasa*) fine is levied for breaking hand, foot and teeth and cutting ear and nose. Similarly one causing injurious wounds, (one who) strikes fatally, (one who) impairs (organs of) movement, eating and speaking, (one who) pierces eyes etc., and (one who) breaks neck, arm and thigh (should be punished with) middle *sāhasa*.

18\. If many persons jointly) assault a man, each one of them (should be levied) double the (amount of) fine laid down before. Articles (forcibly) taken away after a quarrel should be returned and the fine is said to be double.

19\. A person who causes grief should pay the cost of recovery (of the article) and the fine is said to be the same as laid down in the case of a quarrel.

20\. A ferry-man collecting a land-toll should be punished (to pay) ten *paṇas*. A brahmin (going to dine) at the neighbour’s house uninvited, (shall be liable) for the same punishment).

21\. One has to be fined five, ten, twenty and sixty *paṇas* respectively for assaulting, piercing, cutting and breaking the house (of another person).

22\. One should be fined sixteen *paṇas* for having thrown into another’s house, an object, that would cause misery or death to another. The abettor should be fined the middle *sāhasa*.

23\. One should duly be fined two *paṇas* onwards for having caused misery or bleeding injury or breaking the limbs of the body of a small animal.

24\. (One should be fined) the middle (*sāhasa*) and should pay the price for having cut off the genital organ (of an animal) or having killed it. In the case of bigger animals, in these instances, the fine would be double (the above).

25\. The fine is forty (*paṇas*) for lopping the branches, trunk of the tree or the whole tree that is growing and providing sustenance.

26\. One who causes another to indulge in a violent act shall have to pay double the fine and one who says that he would pay (if fine is imposed) and causes another to do (a violent act) (shall be required to pay) four times (that fine).

27-28. It has been fixed that, a person who reviles or shows disrespect to a respectable person, one who beats the wife of his brother, one who does not give the promised gift, one who breaks the summer-house built in the midst of water and one who injures the neighbours, shall be fined fifty *paṇas*.

29-32. One who copulates with a licentious widow, one who assaults (another) uttering abuses, one who abuses (another) without any reason, a man of the low caste touching the men of higher castes, a *śūdra* (a man of the fourth caste) eating the meal at the time of the ceremony of a mendicant and in the divine and ancestral ceremonies, one who makes an improper oath, an incompetent person who does the act of a competent person, one who castrates the bulls or small animals, one who hides a well-known matter, one who destroys the foetus of a servant woman, one who disregards any one of the following—father, son, sister, brother, husband or wife, preceptor and pupil, that has not been degraded, shall be fined a hundred (*paṇas*).

33\. A washerman who wears the dress of others (given to him for washing) should be fined three *paṇas*. It is ten *paṇas* if he sells them or requests others to take (them) without any charges.

34\. One who deals with those who make false (marks) on weights and measures and make counterfeit coins should be fined the highest (*sāhasa*).

35\. The coin-tester who declares the genuine as counterfeit and the counterfeit as genuine should be fined the first (*sāhasa*).

36\. A physician who gives wrong medical treatment to birds and animals, men (in general) and men of royal (household), should be punished with the first, middle and the highest fine respectively.

37\. (An officer) who keeps in custody a man that should not be kept incarcerated and allows an untried (criminal) to escape, should be fined the highest (*sāhasa*).

38\. One who steals an eighth part (of the real weight) of an article, by means of (false) scale or (fraudulent) measurement, should be fined twenty-two *paṇas*, no matter, whether (the real weight) has been increased. or decreased by that fraction.

39\. One who mixes low-standard (material) in medicines, oils, salts, perfumes, grains and molasses etc. should be fined sixteen *paṇas*.

40\. A thousand (*paṇas*) is said to be the fine (to be imposed) on the artisans who collectively (indulge) in affecting the value (of the goods) (or cause) the decrease or the increase of the wealth.

41\. It is considered to be profitable for the traders to sell or purchase everyday, goods that are dependent on the king.

42\. A trader should take five per cent profit on indigenous goods and ten percent (profit) on foreign goods that are bought and sold immediately.

43\. (A trader), after having added the incidental expenses relating to the goods, to (the price) of the goods, should settle its price with the seller or purchaser.

44\. A trader not delivering the goods to the purchaser from whom the cost has been collected, should be made to pay (the amount) along with the profit or the profit (allowed) on the foreign (goods) if (the goods) have come from the foreign (country).

45\. Goods that are sold (already) could (again) be sold, if the previous purchaser has not taken delivery (of the goods). The defects in the goods due to the purchaser’s fault should be borne only by the purchaser.

46\. In the case of any damage to the goods caused by political disturbances or natural calamities, or due to non-delivery at the desired time, the consequences have to be borne only by the seller.

47\. The fine payable by a seller for the damage or the apparent damage to goods sold through his agent would be double the value of the cost (of the goods).

48\. A trader who has purchased the goods without the knowledge of the decrease or increase (in their prices) should not reopen the negotiation. In case he does so, he should be punished (to pay) one sixth (of the value of the whole stock).

49-50. The profits and losses of traders trading as partners for the sake of profit, (should be divided) proportionately to their shares in the capital, or according to agreement made (at the commencement of the business). (A partner) should make good the loss sustained by him on account of doing the prohibited thing or doing a thing that he has not been asked to do or on account of folly. A partner who has saved (the goods) from destruction is eligible to get one tenth (of the value of the goods).

51\. The king shall take a twentieth part (of the value) of the abandoned goods as tax. The contraband (goods) fit for royal use and sold (to someone) should go to the king.

52\. A deceitful purchaser or seller giving out false measures and going away from the toll office should be fined eight times (the value of the goods).

53\. Relatives and rightful heirs who have come should get the properties of a person on his death or his settlement abroad and the king (should get) in the absence of them (the legal heirs).

54\. The (following) injunctions have been laid down for the officiating priest and ploughman: They should eschew dishonesty. They should not be greedy. They should get the task done by (employing) another in the case of (personal) incapacity.

55\. A thief is apprehended by constables on finding the stolen property in his possession, by (his) foot-print, his past crime and dirty clothes.

56-57. Others that hide their caste, name etc. should also be held on account of suspicion. Persons addicted to gambling, wenching and drinking and those who turn pale and speak in a dry and broken voice (should also be held). Those who enquire about the properties and houses of others, those who wander in disguise, those who spend (much) without income, those who sell lost goods (should also be held).

58\. If one who is held on suspicion for theft cannot expiate (himself), he should restore the stolen property. He should be punished as a thief.

59\. Stolen (articles) should be recovered from the thief and he should be put to death by different (methods). A brahmin (convicted of theft) should be branded and banished from his country.

60-6la. The headman of a village should be held responsible for murder and theft, if (the criminal) has not left his jurisdiction. He should be brought to account in the village where he sets his foot. Similarly five or ten villages within a radius of two miles (of the place) (are held responsible).

61b-62a. Those men who abduct the captives, horses and elephants and those who murder violently should be put on the (iron) stake.

62b-64. A stealer of clothes and a pick-pocket should be deprived of both the hands (ie., hands should be cut off). (Or) for the latter offence, one hand and leg should be cut off. (Putting) a thief or a murderer to death by means of giving food or stimulant, (or by means of) fire, water, *mantra* or weapon is known as excellent punishment. The highest (*sāhasa*) (should be) the punishment for causing abortion/miscarriage by means of a weapon.

65\. The highest or the lowest (fine) (should be imposed) on those who kill a man or a woman. A woman who kills a man by giving poison should be fastened to a stone and thrown into water.

66\. A woman who kills by giving poison or setting fire to her preceptor or offspring should be deprived of her ears, hands, nose and lips and killed by (employing) cows.

67\. Incendiaries of fields, dwelling houses, forests, villages, pasture lands and threshing floors and a person who has had intercourse with the king’s wife should be burnt by fire fed on straw placed around.

68\. A man should be caught by the hair when he is having adultery with other women. The highest (*sāhasa*) is the fine if (the woman belonged) to his own caste and middle fine (is prescribed) if (the woman belonged) to the lower caste.

69a. (But) if (the woman) belonged to the higher caste (than the adulterer), the man should be killed and the ears of the woman should be cut off.

69b-71a. One who forcibly removes the garments covering the waist, breast, navel and braids (of a woman), and one who engages in conversation (with a woman) at an inappropriate place and time and who stays with her (similarly) (is liable to be fined). If it is prohibited for a woman, she has to pay (a fine) of one hundred (*paṇas*) and (if for a man), he (has to pay) two hundred (*paṇas*). (In spite of the prohibition if they indulge in the above crimes), they have to be fined as in the case of adultery.

71b. A person mating with an animal shall be fined one hundred (*paṇas*), and (one mating) with a woman of low caste or with a cow (shall be fined) the middle (*sāhasa*).

72\. A person (who mates) with a slave girl or a maidservant held in captivity, though otherwise fit for cohabitation, should be fined fifty *paṇas*.

73\. The fine is said to be ten *paṇas* if one forcibly copulates with a slave girl. One who mates with a woman of the last caste and a woman mendicant should be fettered and banished (from the country).

74\. A person who adds or omits in copying the royal edict or one who releases a seducer should be fined the highest (*sāhas*).

75a. One who pollutes a brahmin (by mixing) forbidden food, should be fined the highest (*sāhasa*).

75b-76a. One who deals in counterfeit gold and one who sells unclean meat should be maimed and fined the highest (*sāhasa*).

76b-77. An owner who releases the wild boars and horned cattle, though he is capable (of keeping them penned), should pay the first *sāhasa* (as fine). (If it is accompanied) by shouting, (the owner should pay) double (the fine). (A man) who calls an innocent man a thief should be made to pay a fine of five hundred (*paṇas*).

78-79. One who utters undesirable words against the king, one who abuses the same, one who sells things connected with a dead body, one who beats his preceptor, one who divulges his (preceptor’s) *mantra*, should be banished (from the country) with his tongue cut off. The fine for a person who rides the carriage or sits on the seat of the king, is the middle *sāhasa*.

80\. The two eyes should be plucked out in the case of a person who acts hostile to the king or the nation. A *śūdra* living like a brahmin (should be) fined eight hundred (*paṇas*).

81\. If one has been defeated in the proper way, thinks that he is unconquered, he should be defeated (again) when he comes and should be punished (to pay) double the (amount of) fine.

82\. A king who has fined a person unjustly should offer the amount to (lord) VaruṇaGL\_NOTE:178860:} and pay thirty times (the amount) to the brahmins.

83\. Piety, wealth, fame, esteem of mankind, favour, love of the subjects and permanent residence in heaven, dispensing justice even as (people) watch are the seven qualities of a king.

**Footnotes and references:**

[\[1\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/257?reading=1#note-t-178860):

Lord of ocean and righteousness.

## The application of the mantras of the Ṛgveda (ṛgvidhāna) \[Chapter 259\]

***Fire-god said*****:**

1\. I shall (now) describe to you the application (of the *mantras*) of the *Ṛg (veda*), *Yajur (veda*), *Sāma (veda*) and *Atharva (veda*) that yield enjoyment and emancipation when repeated and (are used for making) oblations (as) described by Puṣkara to Rāma.

***Puṣkara said*****:**

2\. I shall (now) describe the (religious) rites (relating) to each one of the *Vedas*. You listen first to the application of the *Ṛg (veda*) \[i.e., *ṛgvidhāna*\] that would yield enjoyment and emancipation.

3\. The repetition of the *Gāyatrī (mantra*)[\[1\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178861) especially with (the practice) of *prāṇāyāma* (regulated breathing), (while remaining) in the water as well as at (the time of making) oblations confers the fulfilment of heart’s desires.

4\. O Brahmin! The repetition of the *Gāyatrī* ten thousand times by a man eating only in the night and bathing many times (during the day), destroys all the sins then and there.

5\. One who repeats (the *mantra*) a lakh times while eating the oblations, becomes fit for emancipation. The *praṇava* (the syllable *Oṃ*) is identical with the Supreme Braman and its repetition destroys all the sins.

6\. One who repeats the syllable *Oṃ* while remaining in waist-deep water and drinks the water becomes free from all sins.

7\. (The *praṇava* consists of) three *mātrās* (syllabic instants), three Vedas, three gods (Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva) and three fires.[\[2\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178862) The *mahāvyāhṛtis*[\[3\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178863) are the seven worlds[\[4\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178864). An oblation made with these destroys all the sins.

8\. *Gāyatrī* is the most excellent (among the *mantras* fit) for repetition. The *mahāvyāhṛtis* are also of similar nature. O Rāma! The *aghamarṣaṇa (sūkta*)[\[5\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178865) (destroyer of sins) should be repeated (while remaining) in the water.

9-11 a. The hymn *agnimīle purohitaṃ*[\[6\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178866) (is sacred) for the Fire-god. One should repeat (this hymn) over a year holding the fire on the head, (performing) oblation three times (a day) with *soma* (juice), living on alms and without lighting the fire (for cooking). Then the seven *ṛks* (hymns) known as Vāyu etc. should be daily repeated devoutly. Thus one will realise all his desires.

11b. One who desires to improve his memory should repeat the hymn known as *sadasaspatim*[\[7\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178867).

12-13a. These nine hymns (beginning with) *anvayo yan*[\[8\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178868) are said to be destroyers of death. One who is a captive or being obstructed should repeat (the hymn) *śunaḥśepaṃ ṛṣiṃ*[\[9\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178869). One becomes free from all sins (by this). One who is sick becomes free from sickness.

13b-14. One who is desirous of (gaining) permanent pleasures and the friendship of the wise Purandara (Indra) should repeat daily the sixteen hymns (beginning with) *indrasya*.[\[10\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178870) One who repeats (the hymn) *hiraṇyastūpaṃ*[\[11\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178871) will cause affliction to the enemies.

15-16a. One who repeats (the hymn) *ye te panthāḥ*[\[12\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178872) will be safe on his journey. One who praises lord *Īśāna* with six Rudra hymns everyday or one who offers oblation to Rudra will have greatest peace.

16b-17a. One who extolls the rising Sun with (the hymn) ‘*ud*’[\[13\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178873) and offers water with folded palms seven times will be able to dispel his mental grief.

17b-18. One who repeats the half hymn *dviṣantaṃ*[\[14\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178874) ending with *yadvi pra* will get his sin destroyed within seven nights. One who desires health or one who is sick should repeat (the hymn) *praskannasyottamaṃ*[\[15\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178875).

19-20. One who repeats the half hymn *uttamastasya*[\[16\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178876) in various postures will get long life; if it is repeated at midday one will get radiance; if (repeated) at sunset one will afflict his enemies. One who repeats the hymns *na vadhaḥ*[\[17\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178877) will destroy his enemies.

21\. One who repeats the eleven *suparṇa*[\[18\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178878) hymns will accomplish all the wishes. One who repeats (the hymn) *ādhyātmikīḥ ka*[\[19\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178879) will get emancipation.

22-23. (One who repeats the hymn) *ā no bhadrā*[\[20\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178880) will get long life. One should look at the rising moon with (the repetition of) the hymn *tvam soma* and worship with the twig in the hand. He will certainly get garments. One who desires (long) life should always repeat the hymn of Kautsa (beginning with) *imaṃ*.[\[21\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178881)

24\. By glorifying the Sun at midday with (the hymn) *apanaḥ śośucad*[\[22\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178882), one gets freed from sin like (a bow) when the arrow is discharged.

25-26. One’s pathway becomes safe by the repetition of (the hymn) *jātavedasa*[\[23\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178883). One gets free from all fears. That person enjoying auspicious things will get houses. This (hymn) destroys the bad dream of the previous night. One should repeat (the hymn) *pramandina*[\[24\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178884) and (a woman) who is delivering a child will do so with ease.

27\. A man will get free from all sins after bathing with (the repetition of the hymn) *upannindraṃ*[\[25\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178885) and offering clarified butter as oblation (while repeating) the seven *Vaiśvadeva* (hymns).

28-29. One who repeats (the hymn) *imām*[\[26\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178886) always will get all his desires fulfilled. One who fasts for three nights and offers the twigs of *udumbara* (tree) dipped in clarified butter with (the repetition of) the two (hymns) *mā nastoka*[\[27\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178887) etc. after becoming pure will cut all the fetters of death and live free from disease.

30-3la. One who having glorified Lord Śambhu with (the repetition of) this hymn with arms raised, binds the tuft into a knot while repeating the hymn *mānastoka*, no doubt, becomes invincible by all beings.

31b-32a. One should worship the Sun daily at the three twilights with (the repetition of the hymn) *citraṃ*[\[28\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178888) holding the twig. Thus he will get the desired wealth.

32b-33. One will destroy the entire bad dream and get good food by the repetition of (the hymn) *atha svapna*[\[29\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178889) in the morning and noon everyday. (The hymn) *ubhe* *pumān* is said to destroy the demons.

34\. One who repeats the hymn *ubhe vāsā*[\[30\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178890) will get all the pleasures. A person repeating (the hymn) *na sāgan*[\[31\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178891) will escape from the murderer.

35\. One who repeats (the hymn) *kayā śubha*[\[32\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178892) will attain caste-excellence, and (the hymn) *imaṃ nṛsomaṃ*[\[33\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178893) will give all the pleasures.

36\. Conveying obeisance with (the hymn) *pitaḥ*[\[34\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178894) one will always acquire riches. Oblation made with ghee with (the repetition of the hymn) *agne naya*[\[35\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178895) also shows the path.

37\. One who repeats *suśloka*[\[36\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178896) will always get a progeny of heroes. One is able to destroy all poisons by (the repetition of) the hymn *kaṅkato na*.[\[37\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178897)

38\. One will get all the pleasures by (the repetition of) the hymn *yo* *jāta*[\[38\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178898). One will get an excellent friend by (the repetition of) the hymn *gaṇānām*[\[39\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178899).

39-4la. (One should repeat) the hymn *yo me rājan*[\[40\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178900) that destroys bad dream. One who commences a journey and faces an unpraiseworthy or praiseworthy enemy should repeat the (hymn) *kuvidaṅga*[\[41\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178901). One will enjoy all the desired pleasures by repeating the excellent hymn *ādhyātmika*[\[42\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178902) consisting of twenty-two verses on the full and new moon days.

4Ib-43. One should offer an oblation of clarified butter with concentrated (mind) repeating the hymn *kṛṇuṣva*[\[43\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178903). One will take away the lives of enemies and destroy even the demons (by this). One should worship daily the Fire (god) with the hymn *pari*[\[44\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178904). The Fire (god) having a face on every side Himself protects that person on all sides. One should look at the Sun, (remaining) pure and (repeating) the (hymn) *haṃsaḥ śuciṣad*.[\[45\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178905)

44-47. A man about to cultivate a field should offer oblations of pot-boiled porridge at the centre of the field as laid down with the five (hymns) *svanī svāhā*[\[46\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178906). A farmer should derive his plough in the approriate manner (and offer oblations) to (the gods) Indra, Maruts, Parjanya and Bhaga. One should then worship Indra and these deities with perfumes, garlands and prostrations (after having worshipped) the ploughshare (saying) (the yoke) has been fastened for the sake of grains. Agriculture will thus always thrive and the work relating to sowing (the seeds), cutting, threshing and ploughing will yield profuse results.

48-49. One will get the desired things from the Fire (god) by (the recitation of) the hymn *samudrāt*[\[47\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178907) One who worships the Fire (god) with the two hymns (called) *viśvānara*[\[48\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178908), surmounts all difficulties, gets undiminishing fame, abundant wealth and unsurpassed victory.

50\. One gets the desired riches by propitiating (the Fire god) with (the hymn) *agne tvam*[\[49\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178909). A person desirous of having progeny should repeat the three hymns of Varuṇa daily.

51-52. (Each) morning, one should recite the three *svasti*[\[50\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178910) hymns, whereby one (will) always secure great prosperity. By the recitation of (the hymn) *svasti panthām*[\[51\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178911) one will have safe journey. One who desires to conquer (should repeat the hymn) *vanaspate*[\[52\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178912), (by which) enemies will be laid down with disease. (By the recitation of the same hymn) a woman having a dead foetus will have a good delivery.

53\. One who is desirous to get rain should employ the hymn *acchāvada*[\[53\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178913) after fasting and wearing wet clothes. It will rain in no time.

54\. A person who desires to have a cow should repeat (the hymn) *manasaḥ kāma*.[\[54\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178914) One who desires to have progeny should bathe (reciting the hymn) *kardamena*[\[55\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178915), after becoming pure and practising vow.

55-56. A man who wants to acquire kingdom should bathe with (the repetition of the hymn) *aśvapūrvāṃ*[\[56\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178916). A brahmin should bathe (standing) on a deer-skin as laid down. A king (should bathe standing) on a tiger-skin and a man of the merchant class on a goat (skin) in the same way. It has been declared that ten thousand oblations (should be done) in each case.

57\. If a person desires to have (the herds of cattle) always undiminshing (in his cowpen), he should worship the cow, the mother of the worlds, in the cowpen with (the recitation of) the hymn *āgāvo*[\[57\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178917).

58\. A king should consecrate the (royal) drum with the three (hymns beginning with) *upa*[\[58\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178918). (By this) he will get radiance and strength and rout the enemy.

59\. One who is surrounded by the demons should repeat the hymn *rakṣoghnam*[\[59\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178919) holding grass in the hand. By repeating the hymn *ye ke ca* *jama*[\[60\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178920) one will gain long life.

60\. One should consecrate the constituents of his army by the hymn *jīmūta*[\[61\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178921) first like a liṅga. Then the king will destroy the enemies in the battle.

61-62. One will gain undiminishing wealth by (the recitation of) the three hymns (beginning with) *āgneya*[\[62\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178922). One may fix goblins by (the repetition of) the hymn *amīvaha*[\[63\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178923) in the night. One should repeat this hymn in danger, difficulty, when caught in a fort, taken as a prisoner, while setting out some time, while running away, or when held as a captive.

63-64a One should fast for three nights with self-control, boil sweat gruel and cast one hundred oblations with that with (the repetition of) the hymn *tryambaka*[\[64\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178924) in honour of (Lord) Śiva. One will thus live happily for hundred years.

64b-65. One should worship the rising Sun and the Sun at the middle (of the day) after bathing and with the hymn *taccakṣuḥ*[\[65\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178925) if one desires to have long life. The hymn (called) *indrā* *soma*,[\[66\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178926) (when repeated), is said to destroy the enemy.

66\. A person who has lost his vow by mistake or on account of association with the *vrātyas*[\[67\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178927), should fast and offer oblation with clarified butter with (the recitation of the hymn) *tvamagne vratapā*[\[68\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178928).

67\. A person who repeats the hymn *āditya*[\[69\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178929) and *samrāja*[\[70\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178930) will get victory in debate. One will become free from great fear by (the repetition of) the four (hymns beginning with) *mahī*[\[71\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178931).

68\. One will get all the pleasures by the repetition of the hymn *yadi* *hyetat*[\[72\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178932). One will destroy his enemies by the repetition of the forty-two *aindra*[\[73\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178933) hymns.

69-70. One gets good health by repeating (the hymn) *vācāmahī*[\[74\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178934). A person who eats food repeating the two (hymns) *śanno bhava*[\[75\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178935) after becoming clean and controlling the senses and touches the heart with the hand will not be attacked by diseases. One will destroy the enemy by offering oblations with (the hymns) *uttamedaṃ*[\[76\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178936) after bathing.

71\. One will get food by making oblation with the hymn *śanno'gnir*[\[77\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178937). One will get free from the defects of the quarters (on journey) by (repeating) the hymn *kanyāvārarṣi*[\[78\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178938).

72\. One is able to subjugate the whole universe by the repetition (of the hymn) *yadetya kavyaś*[\[79\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178939) at (sun) rise. One’s speech gets refined by the repetition of (the hymn) *yadvāk*[\[80\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178940).

73\. One gill get good speech by repeating (the hymn) *vāco vidaṃ*[\[81\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178941). The *pāvamāny*[\[82\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178942) hymns are considered to be most sacred.

74\. The thirty *vaikhānasa*[\[83\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178943) hymns are considered to be extremely sacred. O Foremost among the sages! the *parasva*[\[84\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178944) hymns are said to be sixty-two.

75\. The sixty-seven hymns—*svādiṣṭayā*[\[85\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178945)—are declared as destroyers of all sins, purifiers and conferrers of welfare.

76\. The six hundred and ten hymns of *pāvamānya*[\[86\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178946) when repeated and used for making oblations will enable one to conquer the dread of death.

77\. One should repeat (the hymns) *āpo hiṣṭha* while standing in the water to destroy the fear of sin. A man passing through a desert should repeat (the hymn) *pradevanna*[\[87\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178947) after the control (of senses).

78\. When one is haunted by the fear of death, one will get (the end of) his life quickly. One should repeat the single hymn *prāveyābhi*[\[88\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178948) mentally in the night.

79\. (If it is repeated) at dawn or at sunrise one will get victory in gambling. One who has lost his way will find his way by (repeating the hymn) *mā pragāma*[\[89\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178949).

80-8la. If one thinks that the life of a friend of himself is running out, he should bathe and touch the head of the friend (reciting the hymn) *yatteyam*[\[90\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178950) thousand times for five days. He will thus find him long-lived.

81b-82. A wise man should offer a thousand oblations with ghee with (the repetition of the hymn) *idam medhya*[\[91\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178951). One who desires to have cattle (should do it) at the cowpen and one who desires riches, at the crossroads. One who repeats (the hymn *vayaḥ suparṇā*[\[92\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178952) will acquire wealth.

83\. One will become free from all sins by the repetition of (the hymn) *haviṣyantīyam*[\[93\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178953). His diseases will get cured and the digestive power increased.

84\. (The hymn) *yā oṣadhayaḥ*[\[94\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178954) (when repeated) is a means of securing prosperity and curing all the diseases. One who wishes to have rain should employ (the hymn) *bṛhaspate ati*[\[95\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178955).

85\. (The hymns) *sarvatra*[\[96\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178956) and *pratiratha*[\[97\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178957) are known (to confer) supreme peace. (The recitation of the hymn) *sūta saṅkāśyapaṃ*[\[98\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178958) daily is commended for a person desirous to have progeny.

86\. A person who (recites the hymn) *ahaṃ rudra*[\[99\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178959) becomes an eloquent speaker. The learned person who recites (the hymn) *rāti*[\[100\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178960) in the nights is not born again.

87\. The person who recites the *rātrisūkta*[\[101\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178961) in the night spends the night safely. By doing the recitation of (the hymn) *kalpayantī*[\[102\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178962) daily (one will be able to) destroy the enemies.

88\. (The recitation of) the great *Dākṣāyaṇa*[\[103\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178963) hymn confers longevity and radiance. A person who has undertaken a vow should recite (the hymn) *uta devā*[\[104\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178964), that will destroy the diseases.

89\. When there is fear from fire, one should recite the hymn *ayamagne janī*[\[105\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178965). One should repeat (the hymn) *araṇyānī*[\[106\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178966) in the forests to destroy the fear therein.

90\. (One who recites the two hymns)[\[107\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178967) with devotion to (goddess) Brāhmi (the goddess of speech) (and makes use of) *brāhmī* and *śatāvarī* (the two herbs) together with water or ghee separately will gain intelligence and wealth.

91\. One who desires to conquer his enemy in the battle (should recite the hymn) *māsa*[\[108\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178968). (The repetition of the hymn) *brahmaṇo'gniḥ saṃvidānaṃ*[\[109\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178969) prevents the death of the child in the womb.

92\. After getting pure one should recite the hymn *apaihi*[\[110\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178970), that destroys (the effects of) bad dreams. One gains supreme concentration by the repetition of (the hymn) *yenedaṃ*[\[111\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178971).

93\. (The recitation of the hymn) *mayo bhūrvāto*[\[112\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178972) is an excellent means of securing the welfare of the cattle. One will ward off sorcery or jugglery by (the repetition of) this (hymn).

94\. One should repeat (the hymn) *mahī trīṇāmavaro'stu*[\[113\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178973) for securing one’s welfare on his journey. One should repeat (the hymn) *agnaye vidviṣan*[\[114\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178974), which will destroy the enemies.

95-96. The presiding deities of the houses should be worshipped with the hymn *vāstoṣpate*[\[115\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178975). The procedure relating to the repetition has been told. That relating to the oblation has to be known as different. The (prescribed) fee has to be paid at the end of the oblation. (There will be) expiation of the sin by (offering) an oblation. The oblation done with food appeases by the offer of food and gold as gift.

97-99. The blessings of brahmins will be unfailing. One should bathe outside in every case. Oblations made with the white mustard, barley, grains, milk, curd, ghee and the twigs of the *kṣīravṛkṣa-s*[\[116\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178976), yield all the pleasures. The twigs of thorny (trees), black mustard, blood, poison and stone (are used as oblation) in incantation. *Śaktu*[\[117\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-e-178977), milk, curd, food collected as alms, fruits and roots are the food while offering an oblation. Thus the use of the hymns *of* *Ṛgveda* has been explained.

[\[114\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-t-178974):

Could not be traced.

[\[115\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-t-178975):

Taitt. Sam. 3.4.10.1a.

[\[116\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-t-178976):

The four trees—*nyagrodha*, *udumbara*, *aśvattha* and *madhūka*.

[\[117\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/258?reading=1#note-t-178977):

The flour of barley first fried and then ground.

## The use of the hymns of Yajurveda (yajurvidhāna) \[Chapter 260\]

***Puṣkara said*****:**

1-2. I shall describe the use (of the hymns) of *Yajur (veda*) \[i.e., *yajurvidhāna*\], that yield enjoyment and emancipation. Listen (to me): O Rāma: The great *vyāhṛtis*[\[1\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178978) are considered to be preceded by the syllable *oṃ*. They destroy all sins and yield all pleasures. A wise man should worship the gods with thousand oblations of clarified butter.

3\. O Rāma: This confers the desired pleasures. One who desires peace should offer (oblation) with barley. (One should offer) with sesamum for the destruction of sin.

4\. (One should offer oblation) with grains and white mustard that will confer all the pleasures. (Offering oblations) with the twigs of *udumbara* (tree) is commended for one who desires cattle.

5\. One who desires food (should offer oblation) with curd and one who desires peace (should) with milk. One who desires plenty of gold (should offer oblation) with the twigs of *apāmārga*.

6\. One who seeks a maiden should offer oblation *of* *jāti* flowers that have been strung together in pairs and soaked in ghee. One who desires to have (governorship over) a village should offer (oblations of) sesamum and rice.

7\. The oblations (of the twigs) of *śākhoṭa*, *vāsā* and *apāmārga* (trees) (are commended) for bringing (others) under control. O Son of Bhṛgu (Paraśurāma): (oblation) of twigs mixed with poison and blood (should be made) for causing the death of one after becoming sick.

8-9. One who is angry (should act) perfectly in the above manner in order to kill his enemies. O Brahmin: After having made an image of the king made up of rice one should offer a thousand oblations. The king will thus be subjected to one’s control. Flowers (are to be used) by one who desires clothes. (The offering of) *dūrvā* (grass) destroys disease.

10\. It is laid down that strong scents (should be used) by one who desires to gain the splendour of a realised soul. Oblation should be offered with the ash of husk and thorns in retaliatory enchantments.

11-12. (In incantation) to cause animosity, the wings of a crow and owl (should be offered). O Brahmin! One should offer the ghee of a black cow to fire at (the time of) the lunar eclipse and partake of it after having mixed it with the residue of powdered *vacā* (a kind of aromatic root) after incantation a thousand times. This will make him intelligent.

13-14a. A peg of eleven inches made of iron or *khadira* (tree) should be buried in the house of the enemy after repeating (the hymn *dviṣato vadho'si*[\[2\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178979). This act of magical incantation for (the destruction of) the enemy has been narrated to you.

14b-15. By the recitation of (the hymn) *cakṣuṣyā*[\[3\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178980) one will get back lost eyesight. (The repetition) of the section (of the hymn beginning with) *upayuñjata*[\[4\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178981) will procure food. One will be free from difficulties by offering oblation of *dūrvā* (grass) (with the recitation of the hymn) *tanūnapāgne sat*[\[5\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178982).

16-18. Oblation made with curd and clarified butter (with the recitation of the hymn) *bheṣajamasi*[\[6\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178983) will cure the sickness of domestic animals. Oblation (made with the recitation of the hymn) *tryambakaṃ yajāmahe*[\[7\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178984) will increase one’s fortune. (One who makes an oblation with this hymn) pronouncing the name of a maiden, will secure that maiden. One who repeats (this hymn) daily when he is stricken with fear, will get free from fears. By making an oblation with the *dhuttūra* flower along with ghee (repeating this hymn), one will get all the pleasures. O Rāma! One who makes an oblation with *guggulu* (a fragrant gum resin) (with the recitation of the hymn) will see Śaṅkara (Śiva) in the dream.

19-20. One will get long life by repeating the section *yuñjate mana*[\[8\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178985). (The repetition of the hymn) *viṣṇorarāṭaṃ*[\[9\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178986) destroys all the obstacles. It is capable of destroying demons. It also confers victory. (The repetition of the hymn) *ayaṃ no* *agniḥ*[\[10\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178987) yields victory in battle.

21-22. (The hymn) *idamāpaḥ pravahata*[\[11\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178988) (when repeated) while bathing is capable of destroying sins. If one buries an iron nail of ten inches length at the threshold (of the house) of a maiden with (the repetition of the hymn) *viśvakarmannu havis*[\[12\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178989) she will not be given (in marriage) to somebody else. One who makes an oblation with (the repetition of the hymn) *deva-savitaḥ*[\[13\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178990) will get food.

23-24. O Knower of virtue! The excellent brahmin who desires strength should do oblation with sesamum, barley, rice and (twigs of) *apāmārga* with (the recitation of) *agnau svāhā* (oblations to fire). O Brahmin! One will win the affection of the people by making a mark (on the forehead) with *gorocanā* (yellow pigment got from the belly of cow) after having made the incantation (of the sacred syllable) a thousand times.

25-28. The repetition of the Rudra (hymns)[\[14\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178991) is capable of destroying all the sins. The oblation (made with that hymn) accomplishes all tasks and ensures peace everywhere. O Bhārgava! Knower of virtue! when the goats, sheep, horses, elephants, cows, men, kings, children, women, villages, cities and countries are being attacked or afflicted by diseases, when there is the outbreak of plague and there is fear from the enemies, then (the offering) of oblation with Rudra hymns with sweet porridge and ghee (will confer) supreme peace.

29-30. One gets free from all sins by offering oblation with pumpkin and ghee (with the Rudra hymns). Excellent man! One gets free from (the sin of) killing a brahmin by eating the flour of barley, barley or alms in the night and bathing for a month outside. One will get everything by offering oblation with (the repetition of) the hymn *madhuvātā*[\[15\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178992).

31\. One will certainly get children by offering oblation (with the recitation of the hymn) *dadhikrāvṇa*.[\[16\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178993) Similarly (oblation made) with ghee (with the recitation of the hymn) *ghṛtavatī*[\[17\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178994) will give life.

32\. (The recitation of the hymn) *svasti na* *indra*[\[18\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178995) would destroy all difficulties (and the hymn) *iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvaṃ*[\[19\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178996) would increase the strength.

33-34. A thousand oblations made with ghee (with this hymn) will ward off ill-luck. (Oblations made) with (the twigs of) *apāmārga* and rice (with the recitation of the hymn) *sruveṇa devasya tvā*[\[20\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178997) will without any doubt free one quickly from the deformities inflicted by incantation. One would get gold by (oblations) with the twigs of *palāśa* with (the hymn) *rudra pātu*[\[21\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178998) (Rudra protect).

35\. One should offer oblations with rice with (the recitation of the hymn) *śivo* *bhava*[\[22\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-178999) (The repetition of the hymn) *yāḥ senā*[\[23\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179000) removes the fear of thieves.

36\. O Brahmin! One who makes a thousand oblations with black sesamum with (the recitation of the hymn) *yo asmabhyamayātīyāt*[\[24\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179001) will become free from deformities caused by incantation.

37\. One will get food by offering an oblation of food with (the recitation of the hymn) *annapate*[\[25\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179002) The repetition of (the hymn) *haṃsaḥ śuciṣad*[\[26\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179003) (while remaining) in the water destroys sins.

38\. (The repetition of the hymn) *catvāri śṛṅgāḥ*[\[27\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179004) (while remaining) in the water will remove all sins. By the repetition of (the hymn) *devā yajña*[\[28\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179005) one will be respected in the world of Brahmā.

39\. One will obtain the favour of the Sun by offering oblation with clarified butter with (the repetition of the hymn) *vasanta*[\[29\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179006). The rites relating to (the use of the hymn) *suparṇo'si*[\[30\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179007) are the same as for the (seven) *vyāhṛtis*[\[31\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179008).

40\. One will get released from bondage by repeating *namaḥ svāhā*[\[32\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179009) three times. By repeating (the hymn) *drupadā*[\[33\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179010) three times (while remaining) in the water will destroy all sins.

41\. The sacred formula *iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvaṃ*[\[34\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179011) is capable of sharpening the intellect when oblations are offered with clarified butter, curd, milk and sweet porridge.

42\. Oblations made with leaves and fruits with (the recitation of the hymn) *śataṃ yo*[\[35\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179012) confers health, wealth and long life.

43\. (The recitation of the hymn) *oṣadhīḥ pratimodadhvaṃ*[\[36\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179013) while mowing and cutting will give returns. Oblations made with sweet porridge (with the repetition of the hymn) *aśvāvat*[\[37\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179014) will secure peace.

44\. One will be released from bondage by (the repetition of) the sacred formula *tasmā*[\[38\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179015). One will get excellent dress by (repeating the hymn) *yuvā suvāsāḥ*[\[39\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179016).

45\. (The recitation of the hymn) *muñcantu mā śapathyāt*[\[40\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179017) is capable of destroying all the enemies. Oblation of sesamum (while reciting the hymn) *mā mā hiṃsīḥ*[\[41\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179018) is capable of destroying enemies.

46\. (Oblations of) ghee and sweet porridge (with the repetition of the hymns) *namo'stu* *sarvasarpebhyo*[\[42\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179019) and *kṛṇudhvaṃ rāja*[\[43\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179020) destroys magic incantations.

47-49. One can control an epidemic in a village or country by making ten thousand oblations of pieces of *dūrvā* grass with (the recitation of the hymn) *kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt*[\[44\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179021). One who is suffering from a disease will be cured and the grief-stricken (will become free) from grief (by this). O Rāma! A person who offers a thousand twigs of *udumbara* (tree)as oblation with (the recitation of the hymn) *madhumānno vanaspatiḥ*[\[45\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179022) will get wealth. One will also get great fortune and victory in litigation.

50-51. One will make the gods rain by offering oblations (of the same) with (the recitation of the hymn) *apāṃ garbhaṃ*.[\[46\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179023) O Knower of virtue! By making oblations of curd, ghee and honey (with the repetition of the hymn) *apaḥ pinva*[\[47\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179024) one will make it rain heavily. (The repetition of the hymn) *namaste rudra*[\[48\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179025) destroys all misfortunes.

52-53. (The above hymn) is also said to ensure all peace and destroy great sins. One who is afflicted by a disease is protected by (the repetition of the hymn) *adhyavocat*.[\[49\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179026) It is also capable of destroying demons, increasing fame, long life and strength. One will be happy by scattering white mustard and repeating this (hymn) on the journey.

54-55a. O Knower of virtue! One will get long life and undiminishing food by worshipping daily the sun morning and evening unweariedly repeating (the hymn) *asau yastāmro*[\[50\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179027).

55b-56. Weapons are consecrated by the six (hymns) *pramuñca dhanvanas*[\[51\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179028). It will frighten enemies in battle. One need not entertain any doubt. (The repetition of the hymn) *māno mahāntaṃ*[\[52\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179029) confers peace on children.

57\. One should offer oblations of black mustard soaked in pungent oil (with the repetition of) the seven sections (beginning with) *namo hiraṇyabāhave*[\[53\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179030) that will destroy enemies.

58\. One becomes a sovereign by offering oblations of a lakh lotuses with (the recitation of the hymn) *namo vaḥ kirikebhyo*[\[54\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179031). By similar (offerings) of *bilva* (leaves) (one will acquire) gold.

59\. One will obtain wealth by oblations of sesamum with (the repetition of) *imā rudrāya*[\[55\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179032). Oblations with *dūrvā* grass (will make one) free from all diseases.

60\. (The hymn) *āśuḥ śiśāna*[\[56\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179033) (is used) in the protection of weapons. O Rāma! It is said to destroy all the enemies in battle.

61\. O Brahmin! Knower of virtue! One thousand oblations of clarified butter with (the repetition of) the five (hymns) *rāja sāma*[\[57\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179034) will cure the eye disease (of a person).

62\. The oblation (done with the hymn) *śanno vanaspate gehe*[\[58\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179035) will destroy the defects of a building. One will not earn enmity with anyone by offering oblations of clarified butter (with the repetition of) *agna āyūṃṣi*[\[59\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179036).

63\. One will gain victory by the oblation of fried paddy (with the hymn) *apāṃ phena*[\[60\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179037). He who has defective sense-organs will get sound ones by the repetition of (the hymn) *bhadrā*[\[61\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179038).

64\. (The hymn) *agniśca pṛthivī ca*[\[62\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179039) (is) an excellent charm. One who repeats the hymn *adhvana*[\[63\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179040) will be victorious in litigation.

65\. (The hymn) *brahma rājanyaṃ*[\[64\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179041) accomplishes the task (when repeated) at its commencement. One will be free from disease by the oblation of ghee a lakh times (with the repetition of the hymn) *saṃvatsaro'si*[\[65\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179042).

66\. (The hymn) *ketuṃ kṛṇvan*[\[66\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179043) will confer victory in battle.

(The hymn) *indro'gnirdharma*[\[67\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179044) ensures fair play in battle.

67\. The hymn *dhanvanā gā*[\[68\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179045) is excellent for the bow wielder. The hymn *yuñjīta*[\[69\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179046) is known (to be used) in consecrating (the bow).

68\. The hymn *āhiratha*[\[70\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179047) should be used for the consecration of arrows. *Bahvīnāṃ pitā*[\[71\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179048) is said to be the hymn for consecrating quiver.

69\. *Yuñjantī* \[*Yuñjanti*?\][\[72\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179049) is said to be the hymn for arranging horses. (The hymn) *āśuḥ śiśāna*[\[73\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179050) is said (to be used) while commencing a journey.

70\. The hymns *viṣṇoḥ krama*[\[74\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179051) (is said to be) excellent for one who boards a chariot. (The hymn) *ājaṅghanti*[\[75\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179052) is said (to be used) for whipping the horses.

71\. One should repeat (the hymn) *yaḥ senā abhitvari*[\[76\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179053) when facing the army of the enemy. The war drums are beaten with (the recitation of the hymn) *dundubhya*[\[77\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179054).

72-73. One will become victorious by offering oblations earlier with these hymns. A wise man who offers one crore oblations with (the recitation of the hymn) *yamena dattam*[\[78\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179055) will soon produce a chariot that will give victory in the battle. The ceremonies relating to (the hymn) *ā kṛṣṇa*[\[79\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179056) are similar to that of the *vyāhṛtis* (*bhūḥ* etc.).

74\. One will get the composure of mind by the repetition of (the hymn of) *śivasaṅkalpa*[\[80\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179057). One will get fortune by making five lakh oblations (with the repetition of the hymn) *pañcanadyaḥ*[\[81\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179058).

75\. One should wear a golden (plate) after making incantations one thousand times with the hyymn *yad ābadhnan dākṣāyaṇā*[\[82\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179059). It will ward off the enemies.

76\. One will not have the fear of thieves by throwing stones and lumps of earth in all the four directions in the house (after repeating the hymn) *imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ*[\[83\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179060).

77\. (The hymn) *parī me gāmaneṣata*[\[84\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179061) is excellent for charming. One who has come to kill will be subdued.

78\. O Knower of Dharma! A person will be brought under one’s complete control soon by giving him food, betels, flowers and other things charmed (with this hymn).

79-80. (The hymn) *śanno mitra*[\[85\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179062) always confers peace everywhere (when repeated). One will be able to charm the entire world by making oblations of all grains (with the repetition of the hymn) *gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ*[\[86\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179063) at the junction of four roads. The hymn *hiraṇyavarṇāḥ* *śucayaḥ*[\[87\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179064) (is used) in consecration.

81-82. (The hymn) *śanno devīr abhiṣṭaye*[\[88\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179065) (is) excellent for conferring peace. There is no doubt that one will appease the planets and get their grace by offering oblations of clarified butter in parts (to the respective planets) with (the repetition of) the hymn *ekacakra*[\[89\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179066). One who makes oblations of clarified butter with the two (hymns) *gāvo bhago*[\[90\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179067) will get cows.

83\. (The hymn) *pravādāṃṣaḥ sopat*[\[91\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179068) is used in the propitiatory rite in the house. (The hymn) *devebhyo vanaspate*[\[92\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179069) is prescribed (for use) in the rite for the consecration of a tree.

84\. (The hymn) *tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ*[\[93\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/259?reading=1#note-e-179070) is known to be the *gāyatrī* for (Lord) Viṣṇu. It is capable of destroying all the sins and granting all the pleasures.

## The use of the hymns of Sāmaveda (sāmavidhāna) \[Chapter 261\]

***Puṣkara said*****:**

1\. I have described the use of (the hymns of) *Yajur (veda*). I shall (now) describe the use of (the hymns of) *Sāma (veda*) \[i.e., *sāmavidhāna*\]. One will get all the pleasures by repeating the *vaiṣṇavī* hymns.

2\. One pleases (Lord) Śaṅkara (Śiva) by repeating the *chāndasī* (Sāman) hymns well. One will get the grace by repeating the *skāndī* and *paitrī* hymns.

3\. (The repetition of the hymn) *yata indra bhayāmahe*[\[1\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179071) is capable of destroying the harmful effects (of incantations). One who has broken the vow of continence will be released (from the fault) by repeating (the hymn) *agnistigmena*[\[2\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179072).

4\. (The repetition of the hymn) *paritoṣaṃ* *ca*[\[3\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179073) is known to be capable of destroying all sins. One who has sold (a thing) that should not be sold, should repeat (the hymn) *ghṛtavatī*[\[4\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179074).

5-6. (The hymn) *adyā no deva savitaḥ*[\[5\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179075) is known to be capable of destroying bad dreams. O Rāma! The foremost of Bhṛgus! It is laid down that the girdle may be tied with the remnant of the ghee that has been sprinkled with (the hymn) *abodhyagniḥ*[\[6\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179076) as laid down, in the case of the women who have a miscarriage.

7\. Then it should be tied on the wrist of the child that is born, with (the repetition of the hymn) *somaṃ rājānaṃ*[\[7\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179077). This will make the child free from all diseases.

8-9. By the use of *sarpasāma*[\[8\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179078) one will not have the fear of serpents. A brahmin will not have any fear from weapons by tying the *śatāvarī* (a herb) after making a thousand oblations with (the hymn) *mādya tvā vādyate*[\[9\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179079). One will get plenty of food by making oblation (with the hymn) *dīrghatamaso'rka*[\[10\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179080).

10\. One who repeats (the hymn) *samamadhyāyantī*[\[11\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179081) will not die of thirst. One will not get a disease by repeating (the hymn) *tvamimā oṣadhīḥ*[\[12\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179082).

11\. One will become free from fears by repeating (the hymn) *devavrata*[\[13\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179083) on the journey. Oblations offered with (the hymn) *yadindro munaye tvā*[\[14\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179084) increase fortune.

12\. O Rāma! Collyrium applied to the eyes (with the hymn) *bhago* *na citra*[\[15\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179085) will increase fortune. There need be no doubt.

13-14. The repetition (of the hymn) *indreti* *varga*[\[16\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179086) will also increase fortune. A man who seeks the love of a woman should make her listen to (the hymn) *pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ*[\[17\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179087). O Rāma! There need be no doubt that she will love him in return. (The repetition of the hymns) *rathantara*[\[18\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179088) and *vāmadevya*[\[19\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179089) increases the divine splendour.

15\. A child should be fed with the powder of *vacā* soaked in ghee daily with the repetition of (the hymn) *indramidgāthino*[\[20\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179090). It will give him good memory.

16\. There is no doubt that one will get progeny after repeating (the hymn) *rathantara*[\[21\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179091) and offering oblations. The hymn *mayi śrīḥ*[\[22\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179092) has to be repeated for the increase of fortune.

17\. The repetition of the eight *vairūpya*[\[23\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179093) (hymns) daily confers fortune. One will get all the desires fulfilled by repeating the *saptāṣṭaka*[\[24\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179094) (hymns).

18\. One who worships cows daily morning and evening (with the repetition of the hymn) *gavyoṣuṇo*[\[25\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179095) unweariedly will always have cows in his house.

19\. One who offers a *droṇa* (a measure) of barley soaked in ghee into fire (with the repetition of the hymn), *vāta āvātu bheṣajaṃ*[\[26\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179096) as laid down will ward off all spells.

20-21 a. Oblations of sesamum with (the repetition of the hymn) *pra daivo dāso*[\[27\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179097) destroys witchcraft. (Repeating the hymn) *abhi* *tvā* *pūrva pītaye* \[*pitaye*?\][\[28\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179098) followed by the syllable *vaṣaṭ* while offering oblations made with perfumed fuel will yield victory in battle.

21b-24. A wise man should make good figures of elephants, horses and men with flour and represent the chief men of the enemy with oily cakes of flour and cut them into pieces with a knife. Then the knower of the sacred formulas should offer oblations (with these cakes) soaked in mustard oil with wrath while reciting the hymn *abhi tvā śūranonumaḥ*.[\[29\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179099) The wise man gets victory in battle by this act. The hymns *gāruḍa*[\[30\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179100), *vāmadevya*,[\[31\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179101) *rathantara*[\[32\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179102) and *bṛhadratha*[\[33\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/260?reading=1#note-e-179103) are without any doubt said to destroy all sins.

## The use of the hymns of Atharvaveda (atharvavidhāna) \[Chapter 262\]

***Puṣkara said*****:**

1\. The application of the hymns of *Sāma (veda*) has been described. I shall describe to you (the application) of (the hymns of) *Atharva (veda*) \[i.e., *atharvavidhāna*\]. One gets peace by offering oblations with the hymns of the peace class.

2\. One will get rid of all the diseases by offering oblations to (the gods of) the remedial class. One will get free from all sins by offering oblations to (the gods of) the *trisaptīya* class.

3\. One will never get fear by offering oblations to (the gods of) the protection class. O Rāma! one will never be born by offering oblations to (the gods of) the *aparājita* (unconquered) class.

4\. One will ward off untimely death by offering oblations to (the gods of) the life-giving class. One will get welfare everywhere by offering oblations to (the gods of) the welfare class.

5\. One will get united with good fortune (by propitiating the gods of) happiness and armour group. One will remove the defects of a building by offering oblations to the class of deities presiding over the foundations of a house.

6\. In the same way one will remove all the defects by offering oblations to (the gods of) the Raudra class. Oblations (are to be offered to) these ten classes in eighteen propitiatory (rites).

7-9. (The goddesses) Vaiṣṇavī, Śānti, Aindrī, Brāhmī, Raudrī, Vāyavyā, Vāruṇī, Kauberī, Bhārgavī, Prājāpatyā, Tvāṣṭrī, Kaumārī, Vahnidevatā, Mārudgaṇā, Gāndhārī, Śānti Nairṛtakī, Śānti Āṅgirasī, Yāmyā and Pārthivī (are the eighteen propitiatory items) that yield all pleasures. The recitation (of the hymn) *yastvā mṛtyuḥ*[\[1\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179104) conquers death.

10\. One will never be afflicted by serpents by offering oblations with (the hymn) *suparṇastvā*[\[2\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179105)! (The hymn) *indreṇa dattaṃ*[\[3\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179106) confers all the pleasures.

11\. (The hymn) *indreṇa dattam*[\[4\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179107) is capable of destroying all obstacles. The hymn *imā devī*[\[5\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179108) is an excellent all-appeasing (hymn).

12\. (The hymn) *devā maruta*[\[6\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179109) confers all the pleasures. (The hymn) *yamasya lokāt*[\[7\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179110) is excellent for removing (the effects of) bad dreams.

13\. (The hymn) *indraśca pañcavaṇijā*[\[8\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179111) is excellent for profit in trade. Oblations offered with (the hymn) *kāmo me vāji*[\[9\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179112) increase the fortune of women.

14\. Oblation offered a lakh times with (the repetition of the hymn) *tubhyameva jariman*[\[10\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179113) and with (the hymn) *agne gobhir na*[\[11\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179114) will promote the intellect.

15\. Offering oblation with (the hymn) *dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa*[\[12\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179115) will ensure the acquisition of land. The repetition of (the hymn) *alaktakajīva*[\[13\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179116) will ensure prosperous agriculture.

16\. (The hymn) *ahaṃ te bhagna*[\[14\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179117) increases fortune. (The hymn) *ye mepāśāḥ*[\[15\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179118) secures release from bondage.

17\. Oblation offered with the repetition of (the hymn) *śapatvahan*[\[16\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179119) destroys enemies. (The hymn) *tvamuttamam*[\[17\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179120) is capable of increasing fame and intellect.

18\. (The hymn) *yathā mṛgamatī*[\[18\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179121) increases the good fortune of women. (The hymn) *yena cehadiśaṃ*[\[19\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179122) is advantageous for conception.

19\. (The hymn) *ayaṃ te yoniḥ*[\[20\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179123) is favourable for progeny. (The hymn) *śivaḥ śivābhiḥ*[\[21\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179124) increases good fortune.

20\. (The repetition of the hymn) *bṛhaspatirnaḥ paripātu*[\[22\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179125) secures safety on the journey. (The hymn) *muñcāmi tvā*[\[23\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179126) is said to ward off untimely death.

21\. One who masters the *atharvaśiras*[\[24\]](https://vedarama.com/en/books/agni-pur/261?reading=1#note-e-179127) becomes free from all sins. I have described to you some procedures relating to some important hymns.

22-24a. The first material for oblations is the twigs of trees suitable for such rites. O Bhārgava! Clarified butter, rice, white mustard, unbroken rice, sesamum, curd, milk, *darbha* (grass), *dūrvā* (grass), *bilva* (leaves) and lotuses are always said to be the materials that promote peace and prosperity.

24b-25. O Knower of righteousness! Mustard oil, blood, poison, twigs of thorny (trees) should be used in magic incantations. One who knows the employment should repeat the sage, deity and metre (relating to the hymns).
